newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends up on slow farmer selling, oversold.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends up on slow farmer selling, oversold.

text.p: Signals the market was oversold and slow farmer selling in the cash market boosted CBOT corn futures to a higher close, traders said.
"Corn is being harvested but there's not much selling and the basis is firmer," said Mark Cermak of O'Connor and Co.
Traders also said talk circulated that corn yields per acre were declining as the U.S. harvest moved into full swing.

But many traders cited the technical angle as central to the corn futures rally Monday and again Tuesday. They cited position squaring and short covering as lending support to the market with fund buying leading the way up.
"As everybody knows, we're extremly oversold and the market was short. We're just evening up before the report," said Paul Haugens, vice president for FIMAT Futures.
USDA at 0730 CDT Friday will release its October crop production and monthly supply/demand reports.

The nine day relative strength index (RSI) for Dec Friday fell well below 20 points, a level generally considered as very oversold. The RSI indicator rebounded Tuesday to close at 33.292, an area still near the oversold plane of 30.
Corn closed 3-1/2 to 4-1/2 cents per bushel higher, with December up 3-3/4 at $2.96-1/2.

R.J. O'Brien bought four million bushels of December, O'Connor and Co bought five million December, Refco Inc bought four million December and Farmers Commodities Corp bought three million December, traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated at 38,000 contracts, down from 45,214 Monday, according to the CBOT.

In corn options, Refco Inc bought 500 December $2.90 calls at 8-3/4 cents and bought 500 December $3.00 calls at 4-3/4 cents, traders said. Prudential Securities bought 500 July $3.30 calls at 11-1/2 cents, they said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 20,000 contracts, down from 24,505 Monday.
